newsitem.title: FRANCE: Drivers' strike shuts down Paris Metro line.
newsitem.headline: Drivers' strike shuts down Paris Metro line.

text.p: A surprise strike by train drivers shut down one line of the Paris Metro underground on Friday, transport authorities said.

They said the line, running east-west through northern Paris, was out of action after the Communist-led CGT union told drivers to walk off the job in protest at working conditions in a suburban workshop.
The strike was the latest sign of simmering low-level worker unrest over government austerity plans and public spending cuts imposed to help France qualify for a single European currency from 1999.
Three trade unions called on Thursday for a 24-hour Paris public transport strike on November 15 to press demands to save jobs, hike wages and improve security to protect staff.

The strike, which could badly disrupt bus and Metro underground railway services, will coincide with a week of CGT protests due to start on November 12 to demand higher pay, protest over job cuts and urge a halt to privatisations.

It will also coincide with the first anniversary of Prime Minister Alain Juppe's announcement of an unpopular welfare reform which triggered a 24-day wave of strikes that crippled the capital in November and December last year.
In other strike action, some 15 truckers used their lorries to block access to fuel storage facilities in the Brittany port of Brest early on Friday in a continuing protest over fuel taxes.
After protesting truckers tied up traffic around Paris and several other western towns on Thursday, Juppe promised that future diesel tax increases would not exceed inflation.

In the southern port city of Marseille, about 100 CGT activists took hostage a mediator chairing talks between the CGT and state officials on the fate of a disused naval shipyard before freeing him on Friday morning, police sources said.

They said mediator Henri Loisel had been treated well while being held. The negotiations, which have resumed, are over union charges that the government has failed to fulfil a pledge for a partial reopening of the shipyard at La Ciotat.
